audit.title: Price Feeds

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: The opening sentence is a clean, self-contained definition of Data Feeds — "data that is aggregated from many data sources by a decentralized set of independent node operators." But it defines *Data Feeds*, not *Price Feeds*, the page's actual title; the implied question goes unanswered.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: One H1, one section, no H2/H3, no tables or bullets (measured: 1 heading, 0 tables, 0 bullets). Fine as a single chunk but there is nothing to scan; the page cannot host multiple retrievable units.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Zero numerals, zero units, and vague quantifiers "many"/"some" flagged. No update cadence, deviation thresholds, heartbeat, decimals, or supported-network counts — all natural specifics for price feeds.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Three internal links to related docs, zero external/primary sources (measured). Reasonable navigation, but no authoritative anchor.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: One good Data Feeds sentence; no crisp "A Chainlink Price Feed is…" statement near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: No JSON-LD, no canonical, no dates (measured; head could not be verified). CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a full read, but no schema was found in served HTML.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code (measured: 0 fenced blocks). A price-feeds page is a prime place for a copy-pasteable `latestRoundData()` read example; its absence hurts agent utility.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Minimal. No "how do I read a price feed," no "what is a price feed," no troubleshooting/FAQ, no lifecycle coverage.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; prose is unambiguous and well-formed. No action needed beyond adding a Price Feed definition to match the title.

audit.summary: This is a thin overview stub — 84 words, one heading, one paragraph — that introduces Chainlink Data Feeds and hands off to three internal pages. Its one strength is clear, fluent prose with a liftable definition of Data Feeds. Its dominant weakness is that it barely covers its own titled topic ("Price Feeds"): no definition of a price feed, no numbers, no code, no query coverage, no schema. As served, it is unlikely to be retrieved or cited for any specific developer question and would mostly lose to deeper sibling pages.

recommendations.title: Define "Price Feed" in the first liftable sentence
recommendations.where: directly under the H1, before the current Data Feeds sentence.
recommendations.issue: page titled "Price Feeds" opens with "Chainlink Data Feeds provide data…" — never defines a price feed.
recommendations.change: Add: "A Chainlink Price Feed is an on-chain contract that reports the aggregated market price of an asset pair (e.g. ETH/USD), updated by a decentralized network of node operators." Then keep the existing Data Feeds sentence.
recommendations.why: engines lift the first self-contained sentence answering the title's implied question; the page currently answers a different question.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/how-to sections and a minimal read example
recommendations.issue: no "how do I read a price feed," no code, no troubleshooting.
recommendations.change: Add H2 "How to read a Chainlink Price Feed" with a complete, imported Solidity snippet calling `latestRoundData()` (interface import, network, contract address), and an H2 "Common issues" covering stale data / `answeredInRound` checks.
recommendations.why: devs and agents query by task and error; symptom/how-to headings win retrieval that a bare overview loses.

recommendations.title: Add concrete price-feed specifics
recommendations.change: State deviation threshold and heartbeat mechanics, `decimals()` behavior, number of supported networks, and link to the feed registry — with real numbers/units where feed-generic.
recommendations.why: quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes for citation.

recommendations.title: Add machine-readable metadata
recommendations.issue: no JSON-LD, canonical, or dates found in served HTML.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD, a canonical URL, and a visible `dateModified`.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and freshness signals raise parseability and E-E-A-T trust.

recommendations.title: Add one authoritative external reference
recommendations.change: Link the OCR/decentralized-aggregation whitepaper or spec alongside the existing internal links.
recommendations.why: primary-source links raise credibility and citation rate.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers "many" and "some" with no numeric backing.
Title/content mismatch: "Price Feeds" page does not define or scope price feeds.
Wall-free but content-thin: an 84-word stub that defers almost entirely to other pages.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; ensure this page is indexed there.
Head metadata could not be verified from the served `.md`; pass raw `<head>` in the CLI to confirm schema/canonical/date presence before treating them as absent.
This page likely loses retrieval to deeper sibling pages (`selecting-data-feeds`, architecture model); strengthen internal links *from* those hubs into a fleshed-out version of this page.
